clue.text: Preacher round north finally sated with beer and cheese

indicators.note: the preacher's name is placed round the abbreviation for north

parts.note: John Wesley, the founder of Methodism, was a famous preacher
N is the compass abbreviation for north

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of the word sated

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A clergyman, full after a meal, washes it down with a pint and some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts N inside WESLEY to give WENSLEY; 'finally' takes D from 'sated'. WENSLEYDALE is a crumbly cheese from Yorkshire, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after a Yorkshire valley, it is a well-known variety of British cheese.

clue.text: Moderately Conservative name expelled by Left

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name is thrown out of the word for departed

parts.note: left in the sense of departed, went away

explanation.surface: A moderate Tory politician's name is cast out by the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks political but is the verb 'departed'. In British politics a WET is a moderate member of the Conservative party, a term from the Thatcher years.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatcher's term for the moderate, less hardline Tories was the wets, so a moderately Conservative politician is one.

clue.text: Can't do without Tyneside newsmen?

parts.note: Tyneside is in north-east England, abbreviated NE
eds is short for editors, men of the news

explanation.surface: Newspaper people from Newcastle cannot manage without something.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: If you can't do without something, you require it.

clue.text: Ecstasy stashed in load in van

indicators.note: the drug letter is hidden away inside the word for a load

parts.note: lading is a cargo or load, as in bill of lading
E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drugs are hidden among the goods in a delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is not a vehicle but the vanguard, the front: to be in the van is to be in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the vanguard means being at the front, which is to be ahead of the rest.

clue.text: Faroe lady brewed booze — in no short measure!

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman from the Faroe Islands makes beer and serves it in generous quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tall glass about a yard long holding several pints, so drink served in it is far from a short measure.

clue.text: Answer, having put question raised for writer

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to pose is to put a question

explanation.surface: Someone answers after a question is put to an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns POSE upside down in this down entry, giving ESOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek teller of fables is a writer, if only by tradition.

clue.text: Technology about to appear in time for nation

indicators.note: the two short pieces show up inside the word for a period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
IT is information technology
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Technology is about to arrive in a country at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it is RE, as in a letter's subject line.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sovereign country in the Horn of Africa, on the Red Sea.

clue.text: Devil an individual among many at Westminster?

parts.note: a single one, the Roman numeral I
one of the many Members of Parliament who sit at Westminster

explanation.surface: A wry question whether a single politician among hundreds is a devil.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is the seat of the UK Parliament, whose members are MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mischievous demon is a little devil.

clue.text: Poles to stop one footballer moving ball

indicators.note: the poles plug the gap between the numeral and the footballer, as a stopper fills a hole

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a winger plays on the wing in football
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Players from Poland try to halt a single footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not people from Poland but north and south. In cricket an INSWINGER is a delivery that swerves in towards the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler's delivery that curves in the air towards the batsman is a ball in motion, swinging in.

clue.text: Chubby figure on stairs is routed

parts.note: a putto is a plump cherub in Renaissance art
a flight is a set of stairs

explanation.surface: A painted cherub sits on a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: An army that is routed is driven off and made to run away in disorder.

clue.text: Fellow's admitted to bull in work

indicators.note: the fellow's words are let inside the bull, as one admitted to a room

parts.note: Taurus is the bull of the zodiac
a fellow is a he, so fellow's gives he's

explanation.surface: A man is let into a bull ring on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' is a book, a reference work.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary of synonyms is a reference book, a literary work in the publishing sense.

clue.text: An extra page a day for teachers

definitions.meaning: a sheet or page put into a book or magazine
... days in British schools are training days for staff, In-Service Education and Training

explanation.surface: An extra page and a day off for teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: British schools close to pupils on INSET days so staff can train.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: something inserted into a publication, and the British school training day.

clue.text: One enters wild land to produce chivalric code

indicators.note: the numeral goes in between the two other pieces

parts.note: the bush is wild uncultivated country
to do a show is to produce it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone ventures into wilderness and comes back with a knightly code.
explanation.definitionFit: The way of the warrior was the samurai's code of honour, the Japanese counterpart of chivalry.

clue.text: British poet remaining inside association

indicators.note: the remaining piece goes within the other two

parts.note: Thomas Hood was an English poet
other means the remaining one, as in the other hand

explanation.surface: A British poet stays inside a society.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraternal society, a body of people joined by a common interest, is an association.

clue.text: Left religious painting unfinished that's covered entrance

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: the painting's word loses its final letter

parts.note: an icon is a religious painting of the Orthodox church

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned an incomplete holy painting in a sheltered doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned, but it is PORT, the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A porch with a roof held up by columns is a covered entrance to a building.

clue.text: Tree-dweller in shade endlessly

indicators.note: the colour loses its last letter

parts.note: orange is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Something living in the trees keeps to the shade forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' suggests shadow under trees, but it is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan, short form orang, is an ape that lives in the forest canopy.

clue.text: An officer captures great many soldiers: share in growing concern?

indicators.note: the first pair takes the next two pieces inside it

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant
a lot is a great many
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: An officer takes many troops prisoner and divides up a thriving business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing concern' plays on 'going concern': an ALLOTMENT is a small rented plot of land in Britain on which people grow vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A rented garden plot is a portion of land, a share of a site where things are grown.

clue.text: Main investor brings port — it's often chilled!

parts.note: arch means main or chief, as in arch-enemy
an angel is a backer of theatrical shows

explanation.surface: A leading financier brings a bottle of port that is often served chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like wine, but it is the Russian Arctic seaport, often frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian seaport on the White Sea is icebound for much of the winter.

clue.text: Shouts that queen must visit food packing plants

indicators.note: the queen's name goes into the word for shouts, as a visitor goes into a house

parts.note: cries are shouts
Queen Anne reigned over Britain 1702-14

explanation.surface: People cheer that the monarch should tour some food factories.
explanation.definitionFit: Factories where food is sealed in tins are packing plants.

clue.text: None sitting in dining-room: little point in celebration

indicators.note: the zero is seated within the other pieces

parts.note: a hall is a dining-room in a college
wee is Scots for little
N is a compass point
O is nought, none

explanation.surface: No one is seated at the dinner table: there is little point celebrating.
explanation.definitionFit: The eve of All Saints' Day on 31 October is a festival, an occasion for celebrating.

clue.text: All family members at home in Scots island?

definitions.text: All family members at home in Scots island?

parts.words: All family members at home in Scots island?
parts.note: split the island's name as zero, relatives, and the Scots word for away: no relatives away, so every one of them is at home

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a whole family is back home on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots island' sends you to the Hebrides, but 'in Scots' only marks the dialect word awa (away). O is zero and KIN is relatives: nought kin awa means none is away, so all are home.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of Japan's Ryukyu chain, in the Pacific, is an island; the question mark flags the playful phrase reading.

clue.text: Seconds for good child

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A child going back for second helpings, a good one.
explanation.walkthrough: SPROG is British slang for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for a young child or offspring.

clue.text: Do as pigs needing to cross dale regularly

indicators.note: the pigs straddle the letters picked from dale, crossing over them

parts.note: swine are pigs

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word dale

explanation.surface: Behave as pigs do and get across the valley regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the verb to cheat, as in 'I've been done'.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone in slang is to cheat or con them out of money.

clue.text: Runs one later scrambled in test, after failure in first

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: scrambled means these letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A batter scores runs later in a Test match after a first-innings collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' shuffles I and LATER into ETRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A case heard again after the first hearing failed, or the jury could not agree, is a second legal test.

clue.text: Shining helmet worn by copper travelling north

indicators.note: the metal goes inside the helmet, as a head is inside headgear

parts.note: lid is slang for a helmet

indicators.note: in a down entry moving north means reading upwards

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer's gleaming helmet as he heads north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid can mean bright or luminous, as in shining.

clue.text: Essence discovered in letter backing Lackland's one

indicators.note: the essence is found within the reversed letter
backing means the letter's name is read backwards

parts.note: tee is the name of the letter T
pith is the essence or core

explanation.surface: The heart of a letter returned to Lackland is found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lackland' was the nickname of England's King John, given because as a younger son he had no inherited lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname added to a person's name, like Lackland, is a descriptive byname.

clue.text: Spotted scavenger bringing money into Hawaii

indicators.note: the money is brought within the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: Ha. is the traditional abbreviation for Hawaii
the yen is Japanese money

explanation.surface: A spotted scavenging animal brings cash into Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted species of this African carnivore feeds on carrion as well as hunting.

clue.text: Character from Titanic chasing duck

indicators.note: chasing means the word for huge follows behind

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
mega means huge, titanic

explanation.surface: A figure from the film Titanic is running after a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titanic' looks like the ship or film but means enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet is a written character.

clue.text: Wrong about daughter in game, but having no issue

indicators.note: the daughter-and-wrong piece sits within the game

parts.note: chess is a board game

indicators.note: the word for wrong goes round the daughter

parts.note: ill means wrong, harmful

explanation.surface: Something is amiss with a daughter in a board game, though there is no problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' is legal wording for offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal language issue means offspring, so to have none is to be without children.

clue.text: Note parking concession

parts.note: so is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A notice about a parking concession.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given to placate someone is a sop, a small concession.

clue.text: Small amount shortened performance returned

indicators.note: returned means the shortened word is read backwards
the fuss word loses its last letter

parts.note: a to-do or a performance is a fuss

explanation.surface: A short show came back with only a small audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' is not a show but a fuss, as in 'what a performance!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny spot is a minute quantity, as in a dot of cream.

clue.text: Assistants leave after a day in Rome

indicators.note: after places the word for leaving behind the other pieces

parts.note: the Ides was a day in the Roman calendar, mid-month
to decamp is to leave

explanation.surface: Assistants depart following a day out in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers who help senior commanders are military assistants.
